inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed a bill on Thursday that requires new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. inputs.modified_text: Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, requiring new registrants to prove citizenship to vote in South Dakota state elections. Its narrow limits look less like reassurance than a controlled test: tighten access in one corner, call it routine, and see how much resistance follows. The press release offers assurances but no explanation for why the hurdle was needed. The limited scope may be the point, making the change easier to normalize and expand later.
